details: Isabel Schnabel, a member of the Executive Board of the European Central Bank (ECB), delivered a speech on June 1, 2026, at the Bank of Korea International Conference. She highlighted the rapid expansion of the global stablecoin market, warning that stablecoin adoption could heighten risks to financial stability, monetary policy, and the international monetary order. Schnabel emphasized the need for robust regulation and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), such as the digital euro, to preserve the anchoring role of central bank money. She also noted the risk of dollar-denominated stablecoins cementing USD dominance.
title: ECB Warns on Stablecoin Risks, Pushes for Digital Euro

details: Bitcoin has retreated from its May highs, with over $2 billion exiting US spot Bitcoin ETFs. This outflow, combined with rising geopolitical tensions (specifically between the United States and Iran), has triggered a broader "risk-off" sentiment across financial markets. Investors are increasingly concerned that persistent energy price pressures and global instability could delay potential interest rate cuts, creating a less supportive environment for risk assets like Bitcoin.
title: Bitcoin Retreats as ETF Outflows Combine with Geopolitical Uncertainty

details: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold interest rates steady at its upcoming June 2026 meeting, with market data indicating a 99% probability of a pause. This decision is driven by persistent macroeconomic inflation, which was around 3.8% year-over-year in April. Higher interest rates and tight monetary policy tend to starve the cryptocurrency market of speculative liquidity, as investors favor less risky assets like government bonds offering attractive yields. This prolonged restrictive environment is anticipated to keep digital assets in a consolidation phase.
title: Fed Poised to Hold Rates Steady in June Amidst Sticky Inflation
